# Interface example: what deck-vs-books writes

<!-- Generated by spike/render_interface_example.py from spike/out/*.json. Do not edit by hand. Rerun the spike, then the renderer. -->

This feature has no screen of its own. Its interface is the Claim and Gap JSON it adds to `out/<room>/redflags.json`, which the readout, the memo and the ask list read. So the prototype is this page: the real output of the spike ([spike/deck_vs_books_spike.py](spike/deck_vs_books_spike.py)) on the Hollis Voice room, on three test decks made from it, on a run with the P&L hidden, and on Brasswick. Nothing below was typed by hand. The renderer copies it from `spike/out/`.

Every claim on this page parsed as the skeleton's `schema.claim.Claim`, and every quote was found by the skeleton's quote checker (`schema/check_quotes.py`, revision `573567f`). The runs are in `spike/out/validate_*.txt`, written by [spike/validate_against_skeleton.py](spike/validate_against_skeleton.py).

The claim ids here are the spike's (`redflags-dvb-001`). In the product they come from `scans.base.Ids` and read `redflags-NNN`.

## 1. Hollis Voice, the real room: every revenue figure matched to a period

Run: `python3 spike/deck_vs_books_spike.py data_room/hollis_voice`. Output: [spike/out/hollis_voice.txt](spike/out/hollis_voice.txt).

As of 2026-09. First revenue month in the books: 2025-01.

| Slide | Deck figure | Period | Books | How the books figure is made | Gap | Within tolerance |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | $2,500,000 | 2026-09 | $2,240,868 | 12 x 'Recurring revenue (subscription plus pilot)' for 2026-09 | 11.6% | no |
| 3 | chart, 21 bars | 2025-01 to 2026-09 | 'Recurring revenue (subscription plus pilot)', 21 months | bar height / tallest bar against month / largest month | 0.4 points of the tallest bar | yes |
| 3 | chart window | 2025-01 to 2026-09 | revenue from 2025-01 | first chart month against first revenue month |  | yes |
| 11 | 3.5% a month (plan) | 2026-10 to 2027-09 | plan columns 3.50% to 3.50% | month-on-month growth of 'Recurring revenue (subscription plus pilot)', plan columns |  | yes |

Unmatched figures: 0. The Hollis Voice deck shows three revenue figures (the ARR, the chart on slide 3 and the plan growth on slide 11), and all three map to a period in the P&L.

Claims:

- `redflags-dvb-001` (flag, `deck_revenue_vs_pnl`): The deck's ARR of $2,500,000 (slide 3) differs from the P&L's $2,240,868 (12 x 'Recurring revenue (subscription plus pilot)' for 2026-09), a gap of 11.6%.
- `redflags-dvb-002` (info, `deck_revenue_vs_pnl`): The deck's revenue chart on slide 3 has 21 bars for 2025-01 to 2026-09; their shape matches 'Recurring revenue (subscription plus pilot)' in the P&L (largest difference 0.4 points of the tallest bar).
- `redflags-dvb-003` (info, `deck_history_vs_metrics`): The revenue chart on slide 3 starts at 2025-01, the first revenue month in the books, and runs to 2026-09 with no month left out.
- `redflags-dvb-004` (info, `deck_revenue_vs_pnl`): The deck's plan growth of 3.5% a month (slide 11) matches the model's plan columns, which grow 3.50% to 3.50% a month. It is a plan, not a period the books hold as actuals.

The ARR claim in full. It is the deck-against-books half of PF2; see the PRD on how it sits beside `deck_claim_vs_named_cell`.

## 3. Test deck: quarters where the books hold months

Output: [spike/out/hollis_voice_chart_quarterly.txt](spike/out/hollis_voice_chart_quarterly.txt).

- `redflags-dvb-001` (flag, `deck_revenue_vs_pnl`): The deck's ARR of $2,500,000 (slide 3) differs from the P&L's $2,240,868 (12 x 'Recurring revenue (subscription plus pilot)' for 2026-09), a gap of 11.6%.
- `redflags-dvb-002` (info, `deck_revenue_vs_pnl`): The deck's revenue chart on slide 3 has 7 bars for 2025-01 to 2026-09; their shape matches 'Recurring revenue (subscription plus pilot)' in the P&L (largest difference 0.2 points of the tallest bar).
- `redflags-dvb-003` (flag, `deck_history_vs_metrics`): Shows part of the history: the revenue chart on slide 3 shows quarters where the books hold months; no month inside a quarter fell.
- `redflags-dvb-004` (info, `deck_revenue_vs_pnl`): The deck's plan growth of 3.5% a month (slide 11) matches the model's plan columns, which grow 3.50% to 3.50% a month. It is a plan, not a period the books hold as actuals.

## 4. Test deck: a chart the script cannot read

The caption stays, the chart is a grey box. The window check still runs from the caption. The bar check becomes a gap. Output: [spike/out/hollis_voice_chart_unreadable.txt](spike/out/hollis_voice_chart_unreadable.txt).

```json
[
  {
    "what": "Not in the room: a readable chart on slide 3",
    "why": "chart image could not be read",
    "would_need": "The numbers behind the chart, or a readable copy of the slide"
  }
]
```

That is BF4, Ostley's annual invoice booked as September revenue. It belongs to the accounting-mislabels slice, not this one, and this feature does not write a claim for it.

## 7. The clean room reads clear

Label `clear`.

- `redflags-dvb-001` (info, `deck_revenue_vs_pnl`): The deck's ARR of $2,060,868 (slide 3) matches the P&L's $2,060,868 (12 x 'Recurring revenue (subscription)' for 2026-09), a gap of 0.0%.
- `redflags-dvb-002` (info, `deck_revenue_vs_pnl`): The deck's revenue chart on slide 3 has 21 bars for 2025-01 to 2026-09; their shape matches 'Recurring revenue (subscription)' in the P&L (largest difference 0.3 points of the tallest bar).
- `redflags-dvb-003` (info, `deck_history_vs_metrics`): The revenue chart on slide 3 starts at 2025-01, the first revenue month in the books, and runs to 2026-09 with no month left out.
- `redflags-dvb-004` (info, `deck_revenue_vs_pnl`): The deck's plan growth of 3.5% a month (slide 11) matches the model's plan columns, which grow 3.50% to 3.50% a month. It is a plan, not a period the books hold as actuals.

Second read of the books: `03_metrics/customer_mrr_by_month.csv` against `Recurring revenue (subscription)` differs in {"2026-08": 15000.0, "2026-09": 15000.0}. In the clean room the pilot is not recurring, but the customer file's `mrr` column still carries its fee. The production check must pick the revenue-row columns that match the P&L line it compares against (see the PRD, DVB-R9).
